chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Video interviews and plans for the Pittsburgh childhood session
summary: She offers a video interview from January 1979 and the opening of the House in 1975; Hughes steers toward her Pittsburgh years.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Opening the interview: introductions, date and place

blocks.x: Okay, we've had a number of digressions since we came to the end of talking about your recording history and what I originally planned to do right after that was to go back from 1979, which is the last thing we talked about right to the beginning of your career, we want to talk about your family and your background and so on in Pittsburgh, and at last we're getting to it.
Maybe I should point out also that you've been very generous in letting the Institute of Jazz Studies make a copy of a video cassette, videotaped interview that you did with Lewis McMillan at NYU.
In January of '79, I think was the date.

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.

the time that I was rehearsing for "My Old Friends" we were getting ready to move into a new theater. So Lewis approached me, he had this -- the students at NYU were on this project and I guess he had sold them the idea of getting me on tape so I went down and we did this together. I have no way of seeing it and I have no equipment to show it on so I was very happy to make that visit down to the Institute of Jazz Studies and we found out that they had equipment and so, except for a little shakiness, I was quite pleased with the interview.
Yes, it's a terrific interview and in fact, what I'm recommending is that we kind of call that interview Appendix No. 5 of this great mass of all history material we've got in here.

Very good. I have another -- it's a cassette video tape that I'd like for you to see sometime in the future. Can't get hold of it now because it's at a local school and we won't be able to get in there until September, but when school opens that will be available also.

Well, that's terrific. I hope we can have a copy of that made as well.

Yes. The kick-off for the House that Jazz Built that was held in 1975 at the Biltmore Hotel at one of Wilma Dobic's Overseas Press Club jazz parties and on that tape you'll see me playing my pocket trumpet.
